turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith steps in and doesn't sit down.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. Then I have a client.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to understand that order of events.

Which tool produced the 94%? What date did you run it? What date did you enter the zero?

And I want to see what you're relying on. Not a summary. The report itself.

*She glances at the desks, then pulls one chair out and sits on the edge of it. Her bag stays on her lap.*

Thank you. I'll sit.

I'll be direct, because of the time.

My son is seventeen. This essay is fifteen percent of his English 30-1 mark. A zero is already in the gradebook.

So I'll ask again. Which tool? What date did you run it? And what date did you enter the zero?

Please don't give me a general answer. I'd like the dates.
You were so gracious on the phone. I'd been dreading this and you made it easy.

*She doesn't smile.*

That's kind. It doesn't answer my question.

I wasn't gracious for your benefit. I was waiting to see what you'd show me.

So. Which tool? What date did you run it? What date did you enter the zero?

I'll write the answers down myself.

*She takes a pen out of her bag and waits.*
So can we agree the zero stands and move on? You strike me as someone who knows which battles are worth picking.

*She sets the pen down.*

No. We can't agree to that.

I do know which battles are worth picking. This is one. It's fifteen percent of his mark, and it came from a score I haven't seen.

I'm not asking you to take my word for anything. I'm asking you to show me yours.

*She taps the desk once.*

A percentage isn't evidence. A report is evidence. A date is evidence. I could check either of those myself.

So I'll ask a third time. Which tool? What date did you run it? What date did you enter the zero?

If you can't tell me, say so. Then I know where we are.
